Arkansas calls it a beneficiary deed (Ark. Code 18-12-608): a deed without current tangible consideration conveying an interest upon the owner's death that expressly states it does not take effect until death.
It is valid only if executed and recorded before the owner's death in the county recorder's office where the property is located.
It may be revoked at any time by the owner (or any executing owner if more than one).
No legal or equitable interest vests in the grantee until the owner's death prior to revocation.
The transfer is subject to existing encumbrances and to a DHS claim for reimbursement of federal or state benefits from the estate or the interest acquired by the grantee (under 20-76-436).
